messages.author: a5b0783aff29974c
messages.subject: Turning this BUGS code into Stan: Defining likelihood of multivariate normal inside model
parts:
I've been looking at this code for hours. Can someone help me.
I am trying to find parameters(tau and mu) of a data generating process of a multivariate normal.
I am attempting to turn this BUGS code from this link  https://people.orie.cornell.edu/davidr/or678/r2winbugs/MultiNormalBug.pdf 
into stan code 

  data {
    int N;
    vector[2] mu0;
    cov_matrix[2] S2;
    cov_matrix[2] S3;
    real y[N,2];
  }

parameters {
  cov_matrix[2] tau ;
  vector[2] mu;
}


model {  
  
  mu ~ multi_normal_prec(mu0,S2);
  tau ~ wishart(3,S3);

  
  
  for(i in 1:N)
  { 
      y[i,1:2]~multi_normal_prec(mu,tau);   // I have a good feeling that the problem is here
    
  }
   
}

Why do I get the error?

SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:


ERROR at line 31

 29:        for(j in 1:2){
 30:          y[i,j] ~normal(0,1) //multi_normal_prec(mu,tau);
 31:        }
            ^
 32:        

PARSER EXPECTED: ";"
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'multivar2' due to the above error.

In addition, I would also like to trace the covariance as oppose to the precision but when I insert  this chunk

transformed parameters{
  Sigma<-inverse(tau)
}

I also get an error.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Turning this BUGS code into Stan: Defining likelihood of multivariate normal inside model
parts:
Sorry you're having a hard time. You want to
seriously pay attention to what the parser tells
you. More inline.

> On Nov 22, 2016, at 9:02 PM, jt...@st-andrews.ac.uk wrote:
>
>
> I've been looking at this code for hours. Can someone help me.
> I am trying to find parameters(tau and mu) of a data generating process of a multivariate normal.
> I am attempting to turn this BUGS code from this link https://people.orie.cornell.edu/davidr/or678/r2winbugs/MultiNormalBug.pdf
> into stan code
>
> data {
> int N;
> vector[2] mu0;
> cov_matrix[2] S2;
> cov_matrix[2] S3;
> real y[N,2];
> }
>
> parameters {
> cov_matrix[2] tau ;
> vector[2] mu;
> }
>
>
> model {
>
> mu ~ multi_normal_prec(mu0,S2);
> tau ~ wishart(3,S3);
>
>
>
> for(i in 1:N)
> {
> y[i,1:2]~multi_normal_prec(mu,tau); // I have a good feeling that the problem is here

This is also going to fail, because y[i, 1:2] is a real array,
and multi-normal requires a vector. So you need to declare

matrix[N, 2] y;

instead.

>


> }
>
> }
>
> Why do I get the error?
>
> SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:
>
>
> ERROR at line 31
>
> 29: for(j in 1:2){
> 30: y[i,j] ~normal(0,1) //multi_normal_prec(mu,tau);
> 31: }
> ^
> 32:
>
> PARSER EXPECTED: ";"

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

What the parser says. It expects a semicolon after statements.
The semicolon on line 30 is in a comment.

> Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name, :
> failed to parse Stan model 'multivar2' due to the above error.
>
> In addition, I would also like to trace the covariance as oppose to the precision but when I insert this chunk
>
> transformed parameters{
> Sigma<-inverse(tau)
> }
>
> I also get an error.

Presumably an error that Sigma doesn't exist. You need to declare Sigma
before you can define it.

This will all work, but we strongly recommend LKJ priors on
correlation matrices coded with Cholesky factors and then scaled
with whatever prior you think makes sense on the scales. Details
in the regression chapter of the manual.

- Bob
